provenance.citation: Shortliffe, E.H. (1976). Computer-Based Medical Consultations: MYCIN. American Elsevier, New York.
provenance.locus: p.247 — therapy CF derivation: RULE069 (cultures=blood → organism=streptococcus CF 0.7) and RULE071 (organism=streptococcus + allergy-penicillin=no → therapy=penicillin CF 0.9). Combined therapy CF = rule.certainty × premise_cf = 0.9 × 0.7 = 0.630.
provenance.notes: Shortliffe 1976 §11.4 p.247 presents the two-step certainty-factor chain as the canonical MYCIN example. RULE069 fires first (streptococcus CF=0.7), then RULE071 propagates certainty: therapy_cf = 0.9 × 0.7 = 0.630. This fixture asserts the numeric value 0.630 with tolerance 0.001 so the paper-grounded harness can verify the algorithm produces the published result.

input.intent: diagnose bacteremia organism and recommend antibiotic therapy

expected.notes: Shortliffe 1976 p.247: therapy CF = rule certainty (0.9) × premise CF (0.7) = 0.630. The terminal conclusion is therapy=penicillin; organism=streptococcus is an intermediate step consumed as a premise by RULE071.
